subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-capable two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity signal, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, parent wake contract, and user-visible channel behavior should it own?
rationale: The remaining work adds recovery policy, config/default behavior, mutating child-run control, and channel-visible failure handling for existing deployments, so automation should not choose the product and compatibility boundary alone.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt this feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity source, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to the session-activity and kill/reap items.

options.title: Prototype default-off
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in watchdog first, with focused live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until maintainers accept defaults.

options.title: Defer to existing controls
options.body: Do not add automatic nudge/kill yet; rely on configured `runTimeoutSeconds`, diagnostics, and future manual kill/reap controls until more policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt this feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity source, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to the session-activity and kill/reap items.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest recent history across subagent registry, spawn planning, and adjacent timeout/control behavior.
